subject.title: [Reliability]: Enforce atomic intent→execution flow to prevent orphan pre-action notices

question: Should OpenClaw define this commit-or-abort guarantee as part of a broader structured process-events/run-state contract, or as a separate agent-run transaction API?
rationale: The missing contract is source-proven, but the fix sets public lifecycle semantics across protocol, runtime, sessions, SDK/UI clients, plugin-visible surfaces, and possibly policy/config behavior.

options.title: Unify With Process Events
options.body: Make begin, execution evidence, commit, abort, and blocker semantics part of one structured lifecycle/process-events design so clients get a single progress source of truth.

options.title: Create Separate Run Transaction API
options.body: Add a distinct run.begin/run.exec/run.commit/run.abort contract and document how it composes with existing lifecycle, item, plan, and process streams.

options.title: Keep Adjacent Safeguards Only
options.body: Treat strict-agentic retries, liveness states, and no-fake-progress tests as sufficient, then narrow this issue to documentation or telemetry follow-up.

recommendation.title: Unify With Process Events
recommendation.body: Make begin, execution evidence, commit, abort, and blocker semantics part of one structured lifecycle/process-events design so clients get a single progress source of truth.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the prior product-contract keep-open review and has the strongest adjacent lifecycle/event history in this area.
